jobs.title: SENIOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (SPECIALIST) Fire & Landscape Ecologist
jobs.description:
Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) (Fire & Landscape Ecologist) 

CA Coastal Commission 

$8,055.00 - $11,269.00 per Month New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable. 

Final Filing Date: 12/1/2026 

The California Coastal Commission is seeking two Senior Environmental Scientists (Specialists) to join its Ecology Team (Technical Services Unit) at its offices in San Francisco, Santa Cruz, or Long Beach. These positions will primarily focus on the relationship between wildfire and coastal ecology as relates to vegetation management for fuel reduction, ecological health and restoration, and resilience work across a range of ecosystems, including forests, woodlands, shrublands, grasslands, and wetlands throughout California's coastal zone, which extends inland from the shoreline at variable distances up to more than five miles in some areas. It is anticipated that one position will focus on the northern portion of the state, and the other on the southern. 

The Ecology Team generally supports the Commission and its staff with technical review and analysis of potential effects on the coast's sensitive natural resources associated with proposed development projects. Under the direction of the Ecology Team Manager, the successful incumbents will be integrated into the existing team of six ecologists and work with Commission staff to address ecological issues raised in the Commission's policy, planning, and regulatory work as relates to wildfire resilience and risk reduction efforts. This work will focus on understanding and addressing the ecological effects of vegetation management for fuel reduction and wildfire resilience, including through ecological restoration, throughout California's coastal zone. It will necessitate cooperation with other scientific and technical teams such as Mapping and Water Quality, coordination with the Commission's Statewide Planning Unit, and provision of scientific support to staff and the Commission. It will also involve programmatic coordination to streamline natural resource protection along infrastructure corridors associated with utilities and transit. Generally, the incumbents will be expected to: review and analyze proposals, including for expedited wildfire mitigation efforts, and a variety of technical reports including CEQA/NEPA documents, technical surveys and memoranda, restoration and mitigation plans, and scientific literature; conduct research and investigations often involving complex environmental conditions and circumstances; identify problems including potential adverse impacts to coastal resources and means to avoid and minimize these; factor in climate change dynamics relative to environmental considerations; coordinate with other federal, state, and local agencies; and, make recommendations for conformance with the natural resource policies of the Coastal Act, relevant certified plans (e.g., Local Coastal Plans, Public Works Plans), and Environmental Protection Plans. 

Key functions of the job include: analyzing proposed fire resilience and risk reduction work for consistency with applicable Coastal Act policies and/or standards associated with applicable Environmental Protection Plans; tracking topical scientific literature including white papers and peer-reviewed publications; guiding related policy based on scientific understanding of the issues and existing frameworks; developing recommendations on how to avoid and minimize adverse impacts to native habitat (including for communities and species) associated with fuel reduction and vegetation management efforts across the landscape while advancing ecological resilience; contributing to the development of recommendations for Commission regulatory action, including advisories, staff reports, permit conditions, and planning documents; communicating with project proponents; updating and maintaining a spatial database of authorized fire resilience and risk reduction work and conducting geospatial analyses; reviewing monitoring and mitigation plans and reports; conducting site visits and inspections to evaluate on-the-ground ecological conditions; writing technical memoranda to support and accompany staff reports and recommendations; and providing technical presentations at public meetings. The incumbents may also represent the Commission staff on multi-agency work groups, task forces, and similar entities; and coordinate with staff of local, state, and federal agencies; the legislature; stakeholder groups; and the broader public. 

These positions offer considerable opportunity for developing and contributing expertise on a range of ecosystems as well as relevant and emerging issues related to coastal ecology and wildfire resilience in California's coastal landscape. 

You will find additional information about the job in the Duty Statement. 

Guided by the California Coastal Act of 1976, the California Coastal Commission is a small state agency responsible for protecting and enhancing California's coast and ocean resources. It does so through careful planning and regulation of environmentally-sustainable development within offshore waters and on land along the California coast, rigorous use of science, strong public participation, education, and effective intergovernmental coordination. The Commission also has authority under the federal Coastal Zone Management Act to review federal and federally-permitted activities such as dredging, military training exercises, wildland management, and highway projects that affect resources of the coastal zone. 

The California Coastal Commission values diversity at all levels of the organization and is committed to fostering an environment in which employees from a variety of backgrounds, cultures, and personal experiences are welcomed and can thrive. jobs.title: Environmental Health Specialist I/II/Senior
jobs.description:
Posting number: 2026-00256

Department: Environmental Health

Job classification: Environmental Health Specialist I

Posting type: Open

Categories: Environmental Services

Summary

The Tehama County Environmental Health Department's 
mission is to protect health, prevent disease and promote a safe environment for all persons in Tehama County.Click here to learn more about the Tehama County Environmental Health DepartmentClick here to learn more about Tehama County!SALARY

(A-E Steps)

Environmental Health Specialist I: 

 $27.57 - $33.51 Hourly/$2,205.60 – $2,680.80 Bi-Weekly

Environmental Health Specialist II: 

$30.43 - $36.99 Hourly/$2,434.40 - $2,959.20 Bi-Weekly

Environmental Health Specialist Senior:

$36.17 - $43.97 Hourly/$2,893.60 - $3,517.60 Bi-Weekly

Environmental Health Specialist I: Entry-level - The incumbent learns to perform a variety of duties for the purpose of preventing environmental health hazards and promoting and protecting public health and the environment.
Environmental Health Specialist II: Mid-level - Performs investigations and inspections relating to the enforcement of environmental health laws and regulations.
Environmental Health Specialist Senior: Supervisory-level- Develops, implements and manages a variety of complex environmental health programs, for the purpose of preventing environmental health hazards and promoting and protecting public health and the environment.Examples of duties

Environmental Health Specialist I: Conducts supervised inspections of various facilities, including but not limited to food handling and preparation establishments, schools, hospitals, detention centers, water supply and sewage disposal systems, solid waste facilities, recreation/pool facilities and other public/private facilities, to monitor compliance with all applicable laws, codes and standards of sanitation. 
Environmental Health Specialist II: 
In addition to the above: Assists in planning, coordinating and managing the daily operations of one or more environmental health programs as assigned; functions as a resource specialist in assigned program(s) to develop environmental health policies and procedures and to recommend local ordinances and standards.
Environmental Health Specialist Senior: 
In addition to the above:Guides and assists Environmental Health Specialists and/or Aides; provides training, counseling and professional assistance on technical skills and professional responsibilities; identifies training needs and provides training for staff; assures training programs meet goals; serves as liaison between the Department and various organizations and agencies; serves on committees and task forces.Click on the position title below to view the full job descriptions:Environmental Health Specialist I | Environmental Health Specialist II | Environmental Health Specialist SeniorQualifications

Minimum Qualifications: 

Environmental Health Specialist I:

Graduation from an accredited college or university with a Bachelor’s degree with major course work in Environmental Health Science, Biological Science, Chemistry, Physics, Microbiology, Public Health or related field Possession of a valid letter of eligibility indicating acceptance of educational requirements issued by the State of California Department of Public HealthEnvironmental Health Specialist II:

Graduation from an accredited college or university with a Bachelor’s degree with major course work in Environmental Health Science, Biological Science, Chemistry, Physics, Microbiology, Public Health or related fieldPossession of a valid certificate of registration as an Environmental Health Specialist issued by the California State Department of Public HealthEnvironmental Health Specialist Senior:

Graduation from an accredited college or university with a Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Health Science, Biological Science, Chemistry, Physics, Microbiology, Public Health or related fieldPossession of a valid certificate of registration as an Environmental Health Specialist issued by the California State Department of Public HealthThree (3) years of experience at the level of Environmental Health Specialist IIPLEASE NOTE: If you do not currently possess a certification or evaluation letter from the California Department of Environmental Health (CDPH), but believe your education may qualify, click here for more information on how to apply.
 


License & Special Requirements:

Possession of, or ability to obtain and maintain, a valid California Class C Driver License and a satisfactory driving record is required. Individuals who do not meet this requirement due to a disability will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis.

Other certificates and levels of training may be required dependent upon assignment.

Supplemental information

The department is currently recruiting for multiple vacancies. 

In addition, Tehama County is establishing an eligibility list for future vacancies for an Environmental Health Specialist I/II/Senior, as well as vacancies which occur during the life of the eligibility list.

New employees should anticipate being hired at the beginning step of the salary range. Candidates who exceed entry level qualifications may be considered, with approval from 
the Board of Supervisors, for placement at other than A step. Please upload ALL required documents when applying such as, copies of all required degrees and/or certifications as outlined in the job description. Incomplete applications will not be considered.To learn more about Tehama County's Recruitment & Selection process, please click here.For questions about this recruitment please contact:Lori Mueller | 530-527-8020 | lmueller@tehama.govAll offers of employment are contingent upon successful completion of background, fingerprinting, drug test and physical examination provided by the County.
